subject: Stress runbook: stakeholder alignment + schedule for peak-QPS replay
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma@brightlane.com>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposal for stress runbook and scheduling

Emma / BrightLane team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment moving toward the MAP milestone for performance validation (traffic replay + peak-QPS run):

What we covered
- Scope: 3-hour traffic replay using last quarter's production sample to validate tail latency at peak QPS and verify autoscale rules under sustained load.
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 220ms for interactive endpoints; error rate < 0.1% at target load; KV cache effectiveness metric baseline captured.

Proposed MAP milestone (draft) — high level
1) Runbook finalization — owner: BrightLane ops & Redwood (due 2027-05-13)
2) Test data sanity check & sample validation — owner: BrightLane (due 2027-05-14)
3) Dedicated capacity sizing & prep — owner: Redwood infra (due 2027-05-16)
4) Dry run (non-peak) — owner: Redwood + BrightLane (2027-05-20 window)
5) Peak replay (official) — owner: BrightLane (2027-05-22 preferred window)

Dependencies
- Procurement signoff for 2-3 reserved GPU slots (if BrightLane wants Dedicated for predictability).
- Access to sanitized traffic sample (we requested a 10GB CSV subset).
- Network egress whitelist from BrightLane to our replay endpoint IPs.

Scheduling ask
- Please confirm the target peak replay date (we proposed 2027-05-22). If that works we will lock infra and book the runbook review meeting. If not, propose two alternate 3-hour windows next week.

Attachments
- Draft runbook attached: replay-runbook-v1.pdf (contains step-by-step, playbook triggers, rollback plan).
- Small sanitized sample we loaded into our sandbox: test-data-sample.csv

Next steps (my immediate actions)
- Pull in Marissa to confirm Dedicated sizing and availability.
- Put a calendar hold for a 45-min runbook review (tentative: 2027-05-12 10:00 PDT).

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emma Li <emma@brightlane.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposal for stress runbook and scheduling

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can provide the sanitized CSV by EOD Wednesday (2027-05-11). Confirming the 10GB subset is fine.
- Procurement is in the loop and we expect reserved slots approval by 2027-05-18, but we might need the dry run before full procurement completes.

Questions:
1) If Reserved GPU approval is delayed, can you run the dry run on hosted capacity and still produce useful telemetry for sizing?
2) What exact IP ranges do you need whitelisted?

Tentative: 2027-05-22 works as a preferred official replay, but we can be flexible earlier for a dry run (2027-05-20 as you proposed). Please send the runbook review invite and Marissa, looped here, can confirm infra details.

Emma Li
Director of Product Operations, BrightLane Health
emma@brightlane.com

Emma — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below and an updated MAP milestone table with owners and hard dependencies.

Answers
- Hosted dry run: yes — we can execute a dry run on hosted capacity to capture tracing/latency profiles. It won't precisely reflect Dedicated tail behavior (e.g., NVLink latency differences) but will be sufficient to validate test harness, metric collection, and failure modes. We recommend the official peak replay on Dedicated if strict SLO validation is required.
- IP ranges: our replay endpoints originate from 35.203.120.0/24 and 34.72.56.0/24 (please whitelist both).

MAP milestone (revised, please confirm):
*Runbook review (Milestone ID: M1)*
- Owner: BrightLane ops + Redwood (karthik_iyer)
- Target: 2027-05-13
- Deliverable: signed runbook PDF, contact matrix, rollback triggers
- Dependencies: sanitized traffic sample available

*Dry run (M2)*
- Owner: Redwood infra (marissa_cole) + BrightLane ops
- Target: 2027-05-20 09:00–12:00 PDT (3-hour window)
- Deliverable: dry-run report, telemetry dump, trace links
- Dependencies: runbook finalized, basic procurement (purchase order number or short-term credit)

*Capacity prep (M3)*
- Owner: Redwood infra (marissa_cole)
- Target: 2027-05-16
- Deliverable: capacity allocation note (GPU type/count), test harness config
- Notes: preliminary sizing suggestion below

*Official peak replay (M4)*
- Owner: BrightLane (ops lead)
- Target: 2027-05-22 preferred
- Deliverable: full replay artifacts and pass/fail verdict

Preliminary Dedicated sizing suggestion (for procurement planning) — subject to dry-run validation
- Baseline recommendation: 2 x A40 (16GB) with 48 concurrent sessions per GPU (estimate for BrightLane traffic mix)
- If you expect 2x the current peak QPS, consider 3 x A40 or 2 x A100 for headroom
- Expected sustained throughput: ~25k–35k tokens/sec aggregate across GPUs (estimate; will refine after dry run)

I'll attach the runbook v1 (same file) and lock the tentative runbook review for 2027-05-12 10:00 PDT as a hold — can you confirm?

-Karthik

[Attachment: replay-runbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Emma Li <emma@brightlane.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 May 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stress runbook: stakeholder alignment + schedule for peak-QPS replay

Karthik / Emma — looping in infra details and quick confirmation on capacity.

Confirmed availability
- Dry run window 2027-05-20 09:00–12:00 PDT: we have two A40 machines available in the us-west-2 pool and can reserve them for the dry run and the official replay if procurement completes.

Sizing notes (ops perspective)
- For the dry run on hosted capacity: we will run on 2 x A40 (shared hosted), expect noisy neighbor variability. Good for functional validation and telemetry capture.
- For the official replay on Dedicated: recommend 3 x A40 if BrightLane wants <200ms 95th at 2x peak QPS or 2 x A100 for tighter tail latency.

Runbook items I flagged for follow-up
- Health endpoints and metric names (we need the exact Prometheus/Datadog metric keys from BrightLane).
- Flag to disable priority caching for a subset of requests to test cold-path performance.

I'll prepare the capacity allocation note and share a short ops checklist later today. Also attaching a test sample stub we can use for early sanity checks.

Marissa Cole
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: test-data-sample.csv (CSV, 8.6MB)]

Thanks everyone — this aligns with our internal timelines. Quick confirms and next steps from BrightLane: 
- We'll deliver the sanitized CSV by EOD 2027-05-11 (Emma).
- Procurement: tentative PO number expected by 2027-05-18; ops will try to secure short-term credit for the dry run if needed (ops@brightlane.com).
- Runbook review: 2027-05-12 10:00 PDT hold works for our team. Please send calendar invite.
- IP whitelist: we'll add 35.203.120.0/24 and 34.72.56.0/24 today.

One ask: please include in the runbook a short fallback policy in case of unexpected service degradation during the official replay (e.g., immediate rollback to lower concurrency + throttling thresholds). We want explicit timers and contact steps.

Emma
